reason: B is a native inset-grouped list: large title, system toggles, value rows with chevrons, and footer copy that fits the domain ($250 alerts). A uses custom chrome: a small title, bordered cards, an icon on every row, a custom segmented control and five accent swatches. At AX-XL, A breaks 'notification/s' mid-word, while B wraps cleanly.

A is restrained. It has one accent, a calm ramp, a full-width CTA and an inverted CTA in dark mode. B piles on a discount pill, thumbnails, strikethrough, a save badge and installments, and its sticky CTA is off-centre, leaving a dead gap. At AX-XL both break: A's bag button covers the price, but B truncates everything ('Aero', 'Add to…', '$139.') and clips the badge.

A reads as Material on iOS: kebab menu, M3 search pill, check chips, tinted green surfaces, small inline title. At AX-XL its balance splits as '$12,847.' / '33', and the search field and chips get clipped. B uses iOS large-title grouped lists, a dominant balance with de-emphasized cents, and chips that wrap and rows that reflow cleanly at AX-XL.

A misses the brief: it has no monthly/yearly selector, only a yearly trial price shown in fine print. At AX-XL its title is clipped mid-sentence and the features disappear. A shows clear selectable plans with de-emphasized units, an honest 'Save 43%' badge, specific copy and a compact footer at AX-XL. B adds a generic hero icon and icon tiles.

A reads as native iOS: bold large title, inset grouped list, system toggles, a useful footer, and finance-specific copy ($250 alerts, quiet hours). At AX-XL it reflows cleanly. B has a small regular-weight title, indigo accent on headers, toggles and swatches, bordered cards, and example.com content. At AX-XL it breaks 'notification/s' mid-word and its title does not scale.

A has one clear focal number with de-emphasized cents, a large native title and restrained colour. B has a heavy green hero card, a chip row that wraps to a second line, and a floating 'Add expense' button that covers budget rows. B's dark-mode hero becomes a jarring light mint slab. A's real flaw: at AX-XL its trend line overflows horizontally. B truncates and overlaps at AX-XL.

A feels native to iOS. It has a large title, inset grouped lists and a monochrome palette where green is used only for credits, and the balance is clearly the focal point with the cents de-emphasized. At AX-XL it reflows cleanly. B looks like Material Design: a small title, an overflow menu, M3 chips and a mint card. At AX-XL the balance breaks across lines and the chips and search field get clipped.

B has one clear focus: a big safe-to-spend number with smaller cents. It uses few colors, has a clean list and keeps proper dark surfaces. A crams in a hero card, wrapping chips (Reports drops to its own line) and a FAB covering budgets, and its hero inverts to mint in dark mode. At AX-XL both break: A truncates and the FAB covers content, while B shows a visible overflow error stripe.

A: native large title, one dominant 10.3 mi number, a single orange accent, unit de-emphasized, inset-grouped run list. Feels designed and restrained. B: tinted card soup, icon confetti, a hand-rolled header, tiny captions, and a 19 vs 18.6 km mismatch. Its AX-XL single-column reflow is good. A's 'Goal 5 mi' line is ambiguous and its AX-XL chart labels clip.

A collapses at AX-XL: the title is cut to 'Aero', the price to '$139.', and the CTA to 'Add to…'. It also stacks promo noise (OFF badge, Save chip, installments), uses a half-width CTA in a sticky bar, and has a fully tinted surface. B is restrained, with native floating controls, a full-width price CTA, real swatches, a size row and delivery info. B's AX-XL CTA stays readable, but the CTA overlaps the price above it.

A is a tinted card grid: six salmon cards, a pink wash on every surface, the accent used everywhere, and tiny label text. B is restrained and native: large title, one dominant figure, a goal line, an inline stat row and a grouped runs list, with domain-true copy. B loses points for a dead gap under the status bar, a near-black Monday bar, and a flat true-black dark mode.

A is restrained and Apple is clearly the main action, but the top half is an empty void, a stray divider hangs over the buttons, and email is only a button. B is a complete, well-grouped form with realistic copy and a re-tuned dark accent, but its black Apple and green Sign in buttons compete. At AX-XL both wrap acceptably.

B puts its three actions at the bottom in thumb reach and makes Apple the clear primary, with less clutter. A's green Sign in button competes with the black Apple button, and showing the full email form inline makes it busier. B's upper half is very empty. At AX-XL, both wrap button labels and leave the icons stranded; A also clips the divider.

A's demo card shows the product with real content and its dark accent is tuned, but the nested card and chips compete with the headline. A clipped feature row peeks above the CTA, and at AX-XL the card fills the screen, the headline disappears and the mic icon stays tiny. B has a calm headline-first hierarchy, a scannable feature list, and still works at AX-XL.

A fits on one screen, uses its orange accent only once, and has a clear headline-led hierarchy with a primary and secondary CTA. B's product-preview card is more domain-true and its dark mode is better designed. But B uses purple 8+ times, its default-size feature row is cut off under the CTA bar, and at AX-XL the card title truncates while the headline gets pushed off-screen.
